o1.biggest_strength: Targets tier 3 RTO money precisely (holds/cancels unconfirmed tier 3 orders, ₹30 offer only where RTO beats 17%), and covers utility templates for shipped and out-for-delivery to kill the 44% chat load.
o1.biggest_mistake: A ₹30 flat loyalty-weakening bribe plus cancelling tier 3 orders at 48 hours is aggressive; some delivered revenue in tier 3 could be lost, and the offer may train metro-adjacent buyers. The 'Change address' and freeform-after-hours handling is a bit thin.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tie the prepaid incentive to a two-step test (₹30 vs no offer, tier 3 only, holdout) and show the expected net revenue after lost tier 3 cancels, so an owner can approve it without worrying about giving away orders.

o2.biggest_strength: Cleanly written, uses the chat window well (sends prepaid nudge as freeform after confirm), adds a 2pm-midnight agent shift for the after-hours wave, and a no-nudge holdout.
o2.biggest_mistake: Costs are rougher: ₹11.3 lakh and ₹2.6 lakh a week don't square exactly (11.3/4.3 ≠ 2.6), and it calls template 3 'Utility' while using it as a marketing nudge. Also a bit less sharp on the tier 3 RTO targeting—one call and a 2-week trial is softer than O1's hold/cancel mechanic.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fix the weekly RTO arithmetic, make the prepaid template category and opt-in handling unambiguous, and put the tier 3 hold/cancel decision in the main flow rather than a soft trial.

reason: O1's flows are more decisive on the exact place the money leaks—tier 3 COD—and every number ties back to the ₹11.2 lakh RTO pot, so as an owner I'd act on it faster; O2 is cleaner but softer on the money and slightly loose on arithmetic.
